questions.stem: A 65-year-old male patient presented with resting tremors, Bradykinesia, and rigidity and was diagnosed with a case of Parkinsonism. Which of the following drug is not used to treat this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Donepezil

Donepezil is an anticholinesterase drug used in Alzheimer’s disease. All others in the option are used in case of Parkinsonism

questions.stem: Which one of the following drugs does not crosses BBB, but potentiates the activity of Dopamine in the brain?
questions.solutionHtml:
Carbidopa
  • Carbidopa and benserazide are peripheral dopa decarboxylase inhibitors and do not penetrate the blood-brain barrier.
  • They potentiate the activity of dopamine inside the brain by inhibiting the conversion of levodopa to dopamine in the periphery.
  • They do not inhibit the conversion of levodopa to dopamine in the brain.


Lange Katzung, Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 495

questions.stem: A Patient on long term treatment with levodopa therapy develops dyskinetic movements and dose-related fluctuations, best adjuvant treatment for this patient is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Amantadine
  • Amantidine is best adjuvant for dyskinetic movements and dose-related fluctuations in patients on long term treatment with levodopa
  • Amantadine decreases dyskinetic movements
  • Amantadine is less efficacious than levodopa, and its benefits may be short-lived, often disappearing after only a few weeks of treatment.
  • Nevertheless, during that time it may favorably influence the bradykinesia, rigidity, and tremor of parkinsonism.
  • The standard dosage is 100 mg orally two or three times daily.
  • Amantadine may also help in reducing iatrogenic dyskinesias in patients with advanced disease.


Lange Katzung’s Basic & clinical Pharmacology- 14th Edition, Page Number: 491
